claims.claim: GLM-4.5 is an open-source MoE LLM with 355B total parameters and 32B activated parameters
claims.quote: We present GLM-4.5, an open-source Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language model with 355B total parameters and 32B activated parameters

claims.claim: Hybrid reasoning method supporting both thinking and direct response modes
claims.quote: GLM-4.5 and GLM- 4.5-Air both feature hybrid reasoning modes: thinking mode for complex reasoning and agentic tasks, and non-thinking mode for instant responses.
Through multi-stage training on 23T tokens and comprehensive post-training with expert model iteration and reinforcement learning

claims.claim: Comprehensive post-training with expert model iteration and reinforcement learning
claims.quote: comprehensive post-training with expert model iteration and reinforcement learning, GLM-4.5 achieves strong performance across agentic, reasoning, and coding (ARC) tasks

claims.claim: Strong ARC performance; ranks 3rd overall and 2nd on agentic benchmarks with fewer parameters than competitors
claims.quote: With much fewer parameters than several competitors, GLM-4.5 ranks 3rd overall among all evaluated models and 2nd on agentic benchmarks.

claims.claim: Release of a compact GLM-4.5-Air (106B) model
claims.quote: We release both GLM-4.5 (355B parameters) and a compact version, GLM-4.5-Air (106B parameters), to advance research in reasoning and agentic AI systems.

claims.claim: Parameter efficiency: lies on Pareto frontier of SWE-bench Verified vs parameters
claims.quote: where GLM-4.5 and GLM-4.5-Air lie on the Pareto Frontier
We also open-sourced an evaluation toolkit at https://github.com/zai-org/glm-simple-evals to ensure the reproducibility of our benchmark results.

data_disclosure.quote: Our pre-training corpus includes documents from webpages, social media, books, papers, and code repositories.

tokens_disclosed.quote: Through multi-stage training on 23T tokens and comprehensive post-training with expert model iteration and reinforcement learning

coding.note: Main post-trained results tables (3-5) do not say whether comparator scores were rerun or copied, so both are NR. AA-Index is a figure the authors estimated using Artificial Analysis's formula, not an evaluation run by a third party. The RL ablations (curriculum, single-stage 64K, token-weighted loss) and the attention-head observation were not stated as headline contributions in the abstract/intro, so they are not coded as claims. Mid-training/data proportions are given only partially (15T+7T stage sizes, categories), so the data disclosure is coded PARTIAL.
